#Part B1
```{r}
students<-data.frame(
  id = 1:8,
  name = c("Alice", "Bruno", "Chen", "Dana", "Elif", "Farid", "Grace", "Hiro"),
  sex = c("F", "M", "M", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M"),
  midterm = c(78, 85, 92, 67, 74, 88, 95, 89),
  final = c(82,79,96,71,80,91,93,65),
  attendance = c(95,88,100,72,90,85,98,60),
  stringAsFactors = FALSE
)
students
```

#Part B2
```{r}
str(students)
dim(students)
colnames(students)
summary(students)

```

#Part B5

```{r}
students
```

#Part B6
```{r}
classify <- function(score) {
  if (score>= 85) {
    return("Distinction")
  } else if (score >= 70) {
    return("Merit")
  } else if (score>= 50) {
    return("Pass")
  } else {
    return("Fail")
  }
}
```

#Part C1
```{r}
new_students <- data.frame(
id = c(9, 10),
name = c("Ines", "Jamal"),
sex = c("F", "M"),
section = c("C", "A"),
midterm = c(81, 70),
final = c(84, 68),
attendance = c(92, 80),
stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

new_students$average <- round((new_students$midterm + new_students$final) / 2, 1)
new_students$passed <- new_students$average >= 70 & new_students$attendance >= 75
new_students$standing <-
ifelse(new_students$average >= 90, "Honors",
ifelse(new_students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support"))

students_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(students, new_students)
students_all
```

#part C2
```{r}
quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6)
students_all <- cbind(students_all, quiz)
class(students_all)
```

#Part C3
```{r}
m <- cbind(midterm = students_all$midterm, final = students_all$final)
m <- rbind(m, mean = colMeans(m))
m
```

#Part C4
```{r}
bad <- data.frame(wrong_col = 1)
tryCatch(rbind(students, bad), error = function(e) { message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })

#Answer: When the column names are different, rbind may produce an error because it expects the data frames to have the same columns. The tryCatch function catches the error and displays a message saying rbind failed, instead of stopping the program.
```
